solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insect to escape by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word is heard rather than spelt, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to escape is to flee

explanation.surface: A bug that tries to get away and seems to hop off when heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small wingless jumping parasite, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Gentleman, wicked, upset hospital, being only slightly ill

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the joined words upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title given to a gentleman
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: A wicked gentleman unsettles a hospital, though he is barely unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SIR + EVIL as one run, giving LIVERIS, then H is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish describes feeling mildly unwell or queasy, as if from a sluggish liver.

clue.text: A foreign character tucked into what could be dog food

indicators.note: tucked into means the letters are placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a dog could be a pet, an example of one
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign character

explanation.surface: A Greek letter slipped into a tin of dog food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be dog food' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'food'; 'what could be dog' is a pet, an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is a nut eaten as a snack, so it counts as food.

clue.text: Rile sister being naughty — one should keep things clean

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Annoying your sister is naughty, and someone ought to tidy up.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that kills germs keeps instruments clean and safe to use.

clue.text: Element of bitterness leading to one having hesitation

indicators.note: leading to puts the first piece in front of what follows

parts.note: gall means bitterness or resentment
one is I as a Roman numeral
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Bitter feelings lead someone to pause and hesitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallium is a soft silvery metallic chemical element, number 31.

clue.text: Greedily eat egg or bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A choice between breakfast foods: an egg or some bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself with food, eating greedily.

clue.text: Region of the planet that has its attractions

definitions.text: Region of the planet that has its attractions

parts.words: Region of the planet that has its attractions
parts.note: a playful description of the zone around the earth where its magnetic field pulls

explanation.surface: Tourist-board talk about an appealing part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attractions' sounds like tourist sights but means magnetic pull.
explanation.definitionFit: The zone around a planet governed by its magnetic field is where it attracts things.

clue.text: Bar with some judges toping

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bar where a few judges are drinking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to bar or prevent someone from asserting something.

clue.text: English city quietly getting on after break

indicators.note: after places the word on behind the break

parts.note: p (piano) means quietly in music
a rest is a break
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city goes on quietly after a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire in north-west England.

clue.text: Stop crossing river line

indicators.note: crossing means the outer word spans and takes in the other

parts.note: cease means stop

explanation.surface: Halt before you cross the river at the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line made by folding, or a line marked on a cricket pitch.

clue.text: Gear isn't wobbly in engineered frameworks

indicators.note: wobbly suggests unsteady letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Machinery that is steady inside built structures.
explanation.definitionFit: Gantries are overhead steel frames supporting cranes, signals or rocket launches.

clue.text: Be fine splashing about a bit of money — i.e. this?

definitions.text: Be fine splashing about a bit of money — i.e. this?

indicators.note: splashing about suggests letters thrown around, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, a bit of money

explanation.surface: Being generous with cash is what such a person is like.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: someone who splashes money about is generous. Only 'fine' is rearranged, to NEFI; 'Be' stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneficent means doing good, generous and charitable.

clue.text: A live gent's becoming excited as a preacher

indicators.note: excited suggests agitated letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lively gentleman gets worked up preaching.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is someone who preaches the gospel.

clue.text: Salvation Army would have this instrument for greeting

indicators.note: the army's initials would have this word after them, so taking them away leaves it

parts.note: a salute is a greeting, especially a military one

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army band would play this instrument to welcome people.
explanation.walkthrough: SA placed before the answer makes SALUTE, a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute is a plucked stringed instrument with a rounded body.

clue.text: Wild terrain bird occupies shown by quirky illustrator

parts.note: a heath is wild open land
a robin is a common bird
occupies read as 's on, that is, is on top of something

explanation.surface: A bird settles on wild moorland, as drawn by an eccentric artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupies' becomes 'S ON (is on), so the bird's on the heath.
explanation.definitionFit: William Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famous for drawing absurdly elaborate contraptions.

clue.text: Possibly a growing factor helping to make author money

indicators.note: helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that may help an author earn money.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth hormone is one chemical messenger that drives growth in the body.

clue.text: Water from clouds beginning to fall on wicket maybe

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the next
the beginning falls away, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: cirri is the plural of cirrus, a wispy kind of cloud
a wicket is a small gate, so one example of a gate

explanation.surface: Rain from the clouds starts falling on the cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to fall' removes the C of CIRRI, leaving IRRI. A wicket here is a small gate, not the cricket stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land with water.

clue.text: Support good game, making boast

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Backing a fine game gives one something to show off about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' also points to the answer: brag is a card game related to poker.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast about oneself.

clue.text: Documentation makes office assistant get saucy and protest

parts.note: PA stands for personal assistant
pert means cheeky or saucy
to rail is to complain bitterly or protest

explanation.surface: An office assistant gets cheeky and complains.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail of papers is the written records that document a process.

clue.text: Fruit brought by daddy always getting eaten

indicators.note: getting eaten means one piece is swallowed inside the other

parts.note: papa is a word for daddy
ay (aye) is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: Dad brings fruit that always gets eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaya is a tropical fruit with orange flesh, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: Home group featured in small picture

parts.note: in means at home
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A domestic group shown in a small photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture placed within a larger one.

clue.text: Mistake by army officer brings ruin

indicators.note: by puts the two pieces next to each other

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel
a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: An officer's error leads to disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden failure or downfall, a ruin.

clue.text: No shooting it before 12 August? Grumble

definitions.meaning: the red ... shooting season opens on 12 August in Britain, the Glorious Twelfth

explanation.walkthrough: The British shooting season for this game bird starts on 12 August.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is protected until the season opens, and the word also means to complain.

clue.text: Test for local dignitary when May has passed

indicators.note: once May has passed it is gone, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: mayoral means relating to a mayor, a local dignitary
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exam for a mayor once the month of May is over.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination.

clue.text: Composition in middle of test, for example

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: say means for example

explanation.surface: A written piece forms part of an exam, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a short written composition.

clue.text: Remove additional cuts, giving us a let-off

parts.note: extra means additional

indicators.note: letting off the word us means it is released and taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Extra cuts are scrapped, giving us a reprieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving us a let-off' drops US from CUTS, leaving CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull out or take away.
